metadata.title: How to Fix a Leaking Sunroof Drain and Wet Floors in 2006 Volvo S40
metadata.description:
How to fix a water leak in a 2006 Volvo S40. During heavy rain the interior front seats, carpet, and doors would become wet. This was due to a clogged drain tube from the sunroof. This video will show you how to unclog the drain tube and stop leakage.

summary.brief: The video shows how to repair a leaking sunroof drain on a 2006 Volvo S40.
summary.detailed: The presenter explains that water was leaking onto the interior carpet because the sunroof drain tube was clogged. He opens the interior panel covering the drain hose, exposing a brown plastic tube and the small roof‑drain holes. Seeing the tube is blocked, he cuts out the damaged section, splices in a short piece of clear plastic tubing, and pushes the combined tube deeper into the gasket so that more of it sits inside the vehicle. He then blows through the tube to clear any remaining debris, reassembles the panel, and tests the repair by pouring water onto the sunroof; the water now exits cleanly near the front wheel. Finally, he mentions that any water that may have entered the carpet can be vacuumed out to prevent corrosion.

action.detailed: Cut the clogged portion of the drain tube, splice in clear plastic tubing, push the assembly deeper into the gasket, blow through it to clear the blockage, reattach the interior panel, and test the repair by pouring water onto the sunroof.
action.actor: The male presenter (the DIY mechanic) performing the repair

summary_sent_to_llm.description:
How to fix a water leak in a 2006 Volvo S40. During heavy rain the interior front seats, carpet, and doors would become wet. This was due to a clogged drain tube from the sunroof. This video will show you how to unclog the drain tube and stop leakage.

Help support the channel - buy me a coffee!
https://www.buymeacoffee.com/JonathanMorgan

Clear plastic tube on Amazon:
https://amzn.to/3OXFUpk
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The presenter explains that water was leaking onto the interior carpet because the sunroof drain tube was clogged. He opens the interior panel covering the drain hose, exposing a brown plastic tube and the small roof‑drain holes. Seeing the tube is blocked, he cuts out the damaged section, splices in a short piece of clear plastic tubing, and pushes the combined tube deeper into the gasket so that more of it sits inside the vehicle. He then blows through the tube to clear any remaining debris, reassembles the panel, and tests the repair by pouring water onto the sunroof; the water now exits cleanly near the front wheel. Finally, he mentions that any water that may have entered the carpet can be vacuumed out to prevent corrosion.
